narrative: Pull-over-pull against last pull's window (20 to 26 September), the tentative turn flagged then has held: spend firmed slightly to ₹10,467 (from ₹10,326, +1.4%), leads rose to 187 (from 184), and cost per lead eased fractionally to ₹55.97 (from ₹56.12). Within the current window (14 to 20 September vs 21 to 27 September) the read is softer: spend eased 3.2% (₹10,810 to ₹10,467), leads fell 5.1% to 187, CPL rose 2.0% to ₹55.97, and CPM jumped 8.6% to ₹74.35, the sharpest CPM move here in several pulls. 23 September remains a full gap (the raw export exists but its rows don't map to this campaign), so the window is again 6 real days out of 7.

27 September followed 26 September's strong 44-lead day with another solid one: 35 leads on ₹1,989 of spend, the second-best day in the window. Two strong days in a row is the clearest sign yet that the plateau flagged over recent pulls may be turning, though the 8.6% CPM rise bears watching, it is pushing CPL up even while leads hold roughly steady.

Budget kept rotating away from the dominant ad: 'VP_Animated-Static_17July26' fell to ₹6,776 (from ₹7,329 last pull) at a CTR of 0.79% (from 0.81%), now about 65% of spend rather than 71%. The smaller 'VP_Vastu-Shanti_17July26' picked up real traction: spend up to ₹183 (from ₹47) with CTR jumping to 2.73% (from 1.96%), worth a larger test allocation. 'VP_VastuShanti_AD_11Aug2026' stayed small at ₹125 with CTR easing again to 1.30% (from 1.37%).

callout.title: Two strong lead days in a row, but a sharp CPM jump is pulling the other way
callout.body: 26 and 27 September delivered 44 and 35 leads respectively, the best back-to-back stretch in the window, and hook rate ticked up for a second straight pull (25.70%). But CPM rose 8.6% within the window (₹68.47 to ₹74.35), which is why CPL still crept up slightly despite lead volume holding roughly steady. This looks like a market pricing effect rather than a creative or targeting problem.

actions: Keep watching whether the 26 to 27 September pace (44 then 35 leads) continues; two days is a trend, not yet a pattern.
'VP_Vastu-Shanti_17July26' jumped to 2.73% CTR on a small budget (₹183). Give it a larger test spend.

callout.title: Chat decline extends into a third pull as budget keeps drifting toward low-CTR ads

actions: Shift budget back toward 'VP_Baby-Shower_CarouselAD_17Aug26' (2.87% CTR). It has now lost share for three straight pulls while chats fell.
